sources.citation: Pennington, Ryan. 2013. Ma Manda phonology. MA thesis, Graduate Institute of Applied Linguistics, Dallas.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.27: SIL-internal surveys 'are the only information that I am aware of for Nema, Mungkip, Nakame, Sama, and Nuk'; Table 2: Nuk = Potter et al. 2007 survey report with 170-word lists from 2 villages. Erap-wide summary only: 'stress is analyzed in various ways in various languages: quantity-sensitive, quality-sensitive, word-initial, contrastive, and unpredictable.' No Nuk-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.7.11 on Nuk is demographic only ('spoken by 1800 people living east of Boana. There is little dialectal variation'). Sec. 6.1 phonology represents the Erap family by Uri with no stress statement; the only stress remark is 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat' (and contrastive on few words in Suroi). Nothing on Nuk stress.
